prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
The Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system supports continuous production of potable water meeting regulatory requirements, utility operating targets, and customer demand. It is intended to provide operators timely visibility, dependable automatic control, and clear manual intervention points across intake, treatment, laboratory, and distribution functions.

Operational boundary: River Intake Pump Station and Raw Water Screen Channel through treatment, disinfection, finished-water storage control, and discharge to the High Service Pump Header. River Intake Pump Station (local alias: Ironwood; canonical name: River Intake Pump Station) provides the first controlled pumping function, maintaining reliable raw-water availability within approved withdrawal limits. Raw Water Screen Channel belongs to the controlled intake process; debris loading, screen condition, and inlet restrictions affect downstream stability.

Storm Intake Mode is an expected operating state for river conditions requiring conservative intake operation, closer operator review, or modified treatment readiness.

Treatment elements: Coagulant Dosing Skid, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, Chlorine Contact Basin, Clearwell Level Controller, Backwash Recovery Tank, and related instrumentation. Coagulant Dosing Skid controls chemical feed using approved setpoints, observed raw-water conditions, and operator direction. North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are parallel treatment assets presenting local equipment status, headloss indication, turbidity monitoring, and backwash control to plant staff. Chlorine Contact Basin and Clearwell Level Controller are principal control points for disinfection contact management and finished-water storage coordination.

SCADA Historian Server (local alias: Lantern; canonical name: SCADA Historian Server) stores operating data for trend review, compliance support, incident reconstruction, and performance evaluation. Architecture assumes programmable controllers, local panels, operator workstations, analytical instruments, and SCADA Historian Server remain synchronized to plant time standards.

Major external interfaces: electric power service, chemical delivery coordination, laboratory information handling, residuals removal scheduling, and distribution system communications.

New part:
S016: The Chemical Supplier Driver interacts with the plant through controlled delivery procedures that allow chemical inventory changes to be checked before operating setpoints are affected.
S017: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is the normal receiving point for process and compliance samples that support treatment decisions and regulatory documentation.
S018: The Laboratory Technician provides analytical confirmation, communicates unusual results to operations, and helps determine whether process adjustments require additional verification.
S019: The Chief Operator has overall operating authority for plant mode selection, production targets, treatment response, and coordination of abnormal condition response.
S020: The Duty Engineer supports configuration control, evaluates control-system problems, and approves engineering changes that affect operating behavior or documented boundaries.
S021: The Maintenance Planner converts equipment condition information into planned work while coordinating with operations to avoid unnecessary treatment or distribution risk.
S022: The Distribution Dispatcher coordinates finished-water delivery expectations with the plant and communicates demand changes that may affect pumping and storage strategy.
S023: The North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station are treated as distribution interfaces because their operating needs influence finished-water pumping decisions without placing the entire distribution network inside the plant control-system scope.
S024: The Residuals Hauler is considered an operational interface for removal activities associated with treatment residuals and backwash recovery operations.
S025: A Chlorine Residual Alarm is treated as a high-priority condition because it may indicate a public-health risk, an analyzer fault, or a process condition requiring immediate operator assessment.
S026: Routine operation assumes trained staff are available to supervise automatic control, place equipment in safe manual operation when needed, and document deviations through approved plant procedures.
S027: The River Intake Pump Station normally operates in automatic service, with pump starts governed by raw-water demand and available channel depth.
S028: Reduced-capacity service is used when river level, equipment condition, or downstream process demand does not support full intake operation.
S029: Storm Intake Mode is used when rainfall, river rise, debris loading, or upstream runoff creates conditions that require closer supervision of the intake.
S030: The Chief Operator authorizes entry into Storm Intake Mode when field observations or instrument trends show that normal assumptions are no longer reliable.
S031: During Storm Intake Mode, plant staff increase observation of river level, screen loading, turbidity, and pump cycling frequency.
S032: The Raw Water Screen Channel is monitored for upstream level, downstream level, differential level, rake run status, and high-debris indications.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
